title: Ephemeral Admin Assistant & Runbook Slice Compiler for Rapid Support Flows
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Build an Ephemeral Admin Assistant that compiles "runbook slices" (small, self-contained task fragments) into executable, permissioned tasks for first-line support. Goal: decrease time-to-resolution for common incidents by providing curated, auditable tasks that can be dry-runed, executed with RBAC boundaries, and replayed in the sandbox. This ticket scopes the compiler service, RBAC adapters, telemetry hooks, and a thin UI surface for operators.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook Slice Compiler service accepts a YAML/JSON fragment and returns a typed task bundle with explicit inputs/outputs and RBAC policy metadata
Operator can dry-run a compiled slice in the ephemeral sandbox with simulated side-effects (no infra changes) and see telemetry emitted
Execution API enforces per-task RBAC and logs a signed provenance record to the audit log
CLI surface (opsctl) can list available slices, compile a fragment, and launch a dry-run in < 3s for common fragments
End-to-end integration test against staging validates sandbox undo behavior and idempotency for at least 5 canonical slices
implementation_notes: Compiler will reuse fragment schema from ENG-3141593 as the input contract; transform step will normalize to canonical task graph
Prefer a small embedded DSL (YAML-first) rather than heavy templating to make slices readable for support engineers
RBAC adapter maps task labels to roles via a centralized policy service (existing authz API), fall back to require-approval flow if mapping is missing
Telemetry: emit trace/span per compiled step and record tokens-consumed estimate so Console Optimize can attribute cost
Sandbox: leverage existing ephemeral-runlet infra (lightweight container + mock endpoints); implement a no-op enforcement layer for dry-run
Security: sign provenance records with cluster KMS key; store in audit bucket with retention policy configurable by project
progress_updates: 2026-03-10 - Ticket created; initial kickoff with PM and Design. Scoped MVP to compiler + RBAC + dry-run sandbox. (Asha)
2026-03-11 - Spike completed: validated ENG-3141593 fragment schema is sufficient for MVP; prototyped compiler transform in Python. (Diego)
2026-03-12 - Design sync: agreed a minimal UI for opsctl commands (list/compile/dry-run/exec) and a simple confirmation modal for high-risk steps. (Design: Mei)
2026-03-13 - Security review kickoff: security requested explicit signing of provenance and a threat model for sandbox escape vectors; flagged for final review. (Security: Priya)

2026-03-14 - Implemented compiler baseline and unit tests for normalization and RBAC metadata generation; pushed draft PR for early feedback. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-runbook-slices/pull/1234)
review_feedback: PM: prioritize safe dry-run UX over immediate exec to reduce blast radius for MVP (Juan)
Design: simplify fragment authoring by restricting allowed action types for first rollout (Mei)
Security: request additional sandbox hardening and a plan for periodic red-team testing before GA (Priya)
Eng lead: prefer a small Go service for the compiler transform to align with runtime infra; prototype port to follow once Python tests are stable (Sam)
risks: Sandbox escape: if the dry-run environment is not fully mocked, a compiled slice could perform destructive operations during testing
RBAC misconfiguration could allow escalation if task labels are mapped incorrectly to policies
Too much flexibility in the fragment DSL risks creating unreviewable, high-risk slices; needs governance
Telemetry gaps may make it hard to attribute cost regressions to compiled slices in the Console
mitigations: Implement mandatory no-op enforcement in dry-run: network egress and write ops are mocked and fail loudly
Require policy mapping review for new task labels and enforce an approval workflow for unknown labels
Ship a conservative rule set for allowed action types in MVP and a curator flow for expanding capabilities
Add span-level tagging on compile/exec paths so Console can correlate slice executions with cost/latency metrics
next_steps: Finalize compiler API shape and authoring DSL by 2026-03-18 (Diego + Asha)
Address security review notes and produce sandbox threat model doc by 2026-03-20 (Security)
Merge prototype tests and create Go service spike branch for performance/reliability evaluation (Sam)
Add end-to-end staging test that runs 5 canonical slices and validates undo semantics by 2026-03-25
Schedule a cross-functional demo with Support and SRE to gather operational feedback before rollout
